Tick season has begun... 
After two consecutive fairly mild winters, experts are saying tick populations are as high as they've ever 
been. The Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station, which tests ticks submitted by residents, state 
they've already received record numbers of ticks for testing and as high as 50% of the ticks tested have 
tested positive for Lyme or another tick borne disease. Tick bites are typically painless and can often go 
completely unnoticed. While often the bites result in a round rash (or bullseye rash), many times they 
cause no rash at all. So what can you do? 
Get a tick spray program!

You can travel with up to 2 checked pets that are at least 8 weeks old. Please note that as 
capacity is limited, we accept checked pets on a first-come basis. When checking a pet, you'll 
need to: 
• Contact Reservations at least 48 hours prior to travel

• Complete a checklist with an agent

• 10 days of your travel

You can travel with up to 2 checked pets that are at least 8 weeks old. Please note that as capacity is limit
first-come basis. When checking a pet, you'll need to: 
• Contact Reservations at least 48 hours prior to travel

• Complete a checklist with an agent 
• Provide a health certificate 
To ensure the health and safety of your pet, the health certificate you provide must be issued by a vet within: 
• 10 days of your travel 
• 60 days of your return (travel on the same ticket)
